title: Exposure to the Chinese famine in early life and the risk of anaemia in adulthood.
ehr_evidence: We used the data of 2007 adults born between 1954 and 1964 in Jiangsu province from the 2002 Chinese National Nutrition and Health Survey.
summary: Cross-sectional analysis examining the association between early life exposure to the Chinese famine (1959–1961) and the risk of anaemia in adulthood.
key_findings: Fetal exposure to famine was associated with a 37% increased risk of anaemia compared to non-exposed (RR 1.37, 95% CI 1.09-1.71).
The association was stronger in men (RR 1.87, 95% CI 1.21-2.87), overweight/obese individuals (RR 1.75, 95% CI 1.20-2.56), and those with low education (RR 2.07, 95% CI 1.37-3.12).
No significant association between famine exposure and anaemia was found among urban residents.
Total iron intake did not differ significantly across famine exposure groups.
population: 2007 adults born between 1954 and 1964 in Jiangsu province, China
limitations: Lack of iron metabolism biomarkers and menstruation status data
Unassessed regional variation in famine severity
Small sample size in fetal-exposed group limiting subgroup power
Potential selection bias from selective mortality or reduced fertility
Absence of inflammation biomarkers to explore anaemia aetiology
